title: Rav Mordechai (I)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Shabbat 99b relates that Rav Mordechai asked Rava [Hyman says it should read Rabbah, according to Dikdukei Soferim], who answered him, ‘It is a mishnah.’ He came and asked Rav Yosef—Abaye; he answered him, ‘It is a mishnah.’ He said to them, ‘You all spit one another’s spittle!’ They said to him, ‘Do you not agree? Have we not learned—’ He (Rav Mordechai) said to him, ‘Perhaps the mishnah,’ etc.

Hyman writes: From this entire wording it appears clearly that this is not the language of a young student with his elderly teachers but almost of one colleague to another. If so, it is impossible to say that he is Rav Mordechai who was a student of Rav Ashi, in Gittin 59a.
Hyman continues: We also find him in Shabbat 50b: Rav Mordechai said to Rava, ‘Rav Qatina objects’; this Rav Mordechai was truly a colleague of Abaye and Rava, but…

notes.text: The “spittle” phrase accuses them of repeating one another’s answer. The supplied notice stops at “but,” so its remaining argument is missing and stays on hold. Hyman’s Rava-to-Rabbah correction remains attributed.

All nine explicit Rav titles are retained, while Rava, Rabbah and Abaye are unprefixed names. The Rava-to-Rabbah SHOULD READ bracket is Hyman’s reported Dikdukei Soferim correction, not a newly collated reading. The two It-is-a-mishnah replies, plural spittle accusation, genuine Do-you-not question and singular he-said-to-him in Mordechai’s final reply are preserved. The spittle phrase is the accusation of repeating each other’s answer, not being trapped in spit. Hyman owns the strong appears-clearly, NOT-young-student, almost-colleague, IMPOSSIBLE-identity and TRULY-colleague reasoning; no identity split or genealogy is admitted. Gittinנט.. has a double period beside the conventional 59a rendering; Shabbat 99b/50b remain source locators. The supplied Hebrew ends אבל and the English ends but: no missing qualification is invented and the source hold remains. No new primary text, print image or correction-history verification is claimed.

The printed first notice (Hyman, vol. III, p. 902) ends with ‘but’ immediately before the heading Rav Mordechai (II). That next notice begins with the contrasting account of Avimei of Hagronya and Rav Ashi’s academy. The transition is present in print. In the consulted Shabbat 99b, Mordechai receives the same answer from Rava, Rav Yosef and Abaye in succession. Dikdukei Soferim (Shabbat, reader p. 213, note ע) places the printed ‘from Rava’ beside manuscript ‘from Rabbah’. The cited Shabbat 50b passage has Mordechai address Rava about Rav Qatina’s objection, which continues on 51a. Gittin 59a has a dispute referred to Mordechai, whom Rashi calls Rav Ashi’s student. Hyman’s conclusion about the two figures remains his interpretation.
